clientPortals.title: A home for every client
clientPortals.summary: Clients can step into their own workspace, review what’s in progress, and leave a note — without borrowing a teammate’s login.

item1.text: Guest access with a view-only role, so clients see progress without a full seat.

item2.text: A client-ready overview on the start page with the work that matters this week.

item3.text: Switching organizations keeps your place, even with a long client list.

planClarity.title: Plans you can explain in one sitting
planClarity.summary: Checkout and the pricing table now lead with the amount, then the details — so nobody has to decode a spreadsheet on a sales call.

item1.text: The pricing table leads with the price, then the features that come with it.

item2.text: Annual plans show the savings at checkout, not after the invoice lands.

item3.text: Subscription status could lag right after checkout. It now updates immediately.

quietWeek.title: A quieter week of polish
quietWeek.summary: No headline feature — just the empty states, emails, and invite edges that make the product feel finished.

item1.text: Empty members and invitations screens now suggest a next step instead of staring back at you.

item2.text: Invite links failed when the person already had an account. They now drop into the right workspace.

item3.text: Billing emails name the workspace they belong to, so a multi-client inbox stays readable.

workspaceSwitching.title: Switch workspaces without the wait
workspaceSwitching.summary: Moving between clients should feel like changing folders, not reloading the app. This release is about that click.

item1.text: Organization switching stays snappy even with dozens of memberships.

item2.text: We remember the last workspace you had open and take you back there.

item3.text: The org switcher could show a stale name after a rename. It now follows the workspace.

invites.title: Invites that feel like a handshake
invites.summary: The first email someone gets from Acme should name the workspace, the person who asked, and what to do next.

item1.text: Invite emails include the workspace name and who asked you in.

item2.text: First-run setup walks you through creating the first organization instead of dumping you on an empty start page.

item3.text: Expired invites now say so, instead of a generic error.

launch.title: Acme, from first login
launch.summary: The first public release: organizations, roles, and billing in one place — so a team can invite people and charge for work without a side quest.

item1.text: Organizations, roles, and billing live together from day one.

item2.text: A start page for each workspace so teams know where to begin.

item3.text: Self-serve plan changes from the customer portal.

faq.description: Straight answers to the questions teams ask before they start.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions

refundPolicy.question: What is the refund policy?
refundPolicy.answer: If the product is not a fit, request a refund within 30 days and we will process it in full.

cancelSubscription.question: How do I cancel my subscription?
cancelSubscription.answer: Open Billing in your account settings and cancel anytime. Access continues through the end of the current period.

changePlan.question: Can I change my plan?
changePlan.answer: Yes. Upgrade or downgrade from Billing at any time. Changes take effect on the next invoice unless noted otherwise.

freeTrial.question: Do you offer a free trial?
freeTrial.answer: Yes. Paid plans include a 7-day trial so you can evaluate the full product with your team.

item1.quote: We replaced months of auth and billing work with a foundation we could actually extend. Our first paying customers were live in weeks, not quarters.
item1.name: Maya Chen

item2.quote: The organization model matched how we already sell. Invites, roles, and workspace switching just worked — we spent our time on the product instead.
item2.name: Jonas Weber

item3.quote: Clean defaults, clear structure, and nothing fighting us when we customized. It feels like a senior team left us a strong starting point.
